sanskrit: evam uktā vasiṣṭhena śabalā śatrusūdana vidadhe kāmadhuk kāmān yasya yasya yathepsitam
english: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, O slayer of enemies, Śabalā the wish-fulfilling cow granted the desires of each and every one exactly as they wished.

sanskrit: ikṣūn madhūṃs tathā lājān maireyāṃś ca varāsavān pānāni ca mahārhāṇi bhakṣyāṃś coccāvacāṃs tathā
english: Sugar canes and honeys, as well as parched grain, choice maireyā liquors and fine wines, costly drinks, and eatables of every variety—all these she produced.

sanskrit: uṣṇāḍhyasyaudanasyāpi rāśayaḥ parvatopamāḥ mṛṣṭānnāni ca sūpāś ca dadhikulyās tathaiva ca
english: Mountain-like heaps of steaming cooked rice, fine prepared foods and soups, and streams of curds as well.

sanskrit: nānāsvādurasānāṃ ca ṣāḍavānāṃ tathaiva ca bhājanāni supūrṇāni gauḍāni ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Vessels filled to the brim with sweet-tasting confections of various kinds, and thousands of molasses-based sweets as well.

sanskrit: sarvam āsīt susaṃtuṣṭaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanākulam viśvāmitrabalaṃ rāma vasiṣṭhenābhitarpitam
english: Everything was abundantly satisfied; O Rāma, Viśvāmitra's entire army was gratified by Vasiṣṭha, crowded with men joyful and well-fed.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'pi rājarṣir hṛṣṭapuṣṭas tadābhavat sāntaḥ puravaro rājā sabrāhmaṇapurohitaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra too, the royal sage, became glad and well-pleased at that time, as did the king of the foremost city together with his brāhmaṇas and chief priest.

sanskrit: sāmātyo mantrisahitaḥ sabhṛtyaḥ pūjitas tadā yuktaḥ pareṇa harṣeṇa vasiṣṭham idam abravīt
english: Honored together with his ministers and counselors and his attendants, filled with the greatest joy, he spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: pūjito 'haṃ tvayā brahman pūjārheṇa susatkṛtaḥ śrūyatām abhidhāsyāmi vākyaṃ vākyaviśārada
english: "I have been honored by you, O brāhmaṇa, who are worthy of honor; I have been well-received. O master of speech, hear the words I am about to speak.

sanskrit: gavāṃ śatasahasreṇa dīyatāṃ śabalā mama ratnaṃ hi bhagavann etad ratnahārī ca pārthivaḥ tasmān me śabalāṃ dehi mamaiṣā dharmato dvija
english: "Let Śabalā be given to me in exchange for a hundred thousand cows; for, O venerable one, this is a jewel, and a king carries off jewels. Therefore give Śabalā to me, O twice-born—by right she is mine."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhagavān vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ viśvāmitreṇa dharmātmā pratyuvāca mahīpatim
english: Thus addressed by Viśvāmitra, the venerable Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of sages and righteous-souled, replied to the king of the earth.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śatasahasreṇa nāpi koṭiśatair gavām rājan dāsyāmi śabalāṃ rāśibhī rajatasya vā
english: "I will not give Śabalā for a hundred thousand cows, nor for hundreds of crores of cows, O king, nor for masses of silver.

sanskrit: na parityāgam arheyaṃ matsakāśād ariṃdama śāśvatī śabalā mahyaṃ kīrtir ātmavato yathā
english: "She ought never to be abandoned from my side, O crusher of foes; Śabalā is eternally mine, as glory is to one possessed of a noble self.

sanskrit: asyāṃ havyaṃ ca kavyaṃ ca prāṇayātrā tathaiva ca āyattam agnihotraṃ ca balir homas tathaiva ca
english: "On her depend the oblations to the gods and to the ancestors, as well as my daily sustenance; on her depend the agnihotra fire-sacrifice, the bali offering, and the homa ritual as well.

sanskrit: svāhākāravaṣaṭkārau vidyāś ca vividhās tathā āyattam atra rājarṣe sarvam etan na saṃśayaḥ
english: "The invocations svāhā and vaṣaṭ, as well as the various branches of sacred knowledge—all these depend on her here, O royal sage; there is no doubt of this.

sanskrit: sarva svam etat satyena mama tuṣṭikarī sadā kāraṇair bahubhī rājan na dāsye śabalāṃ tava
english: "All of this is truly my own; she always brings me contentment. For many reasons, O king, I will not give Śabalā to you."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhenaivam uktas tu viśvāmitro 'bravīt tataḥ saṃrabdhataram atyarthaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra then spoke words exceedingly more agitated, he who was so skilled in speech.

sanskrit: hairaṇyakakṣyāgraiveyān suvarṇāṅkuśabhūṣitān dadāmi kuñjarāṇāṃ te sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: "I give you fourteen thousand elephants adorned with golden girths and neck-ornaments, decorated with golden goads.

sanskrit: hairaṇyānāṃ rathānāṃ ca śvetāśvānāṃ caturyujām dadāmi te śatāny aṣṭau kiṅkiṇīkavibhūṣitān
english: "I give you eight hundred golden chariots yoked with four white horses each, adorned with little bells.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ deśajātānāṃ kulajānāṃ mahaujasām sahasram ekaṃ daśa ca dadāmi tava suvrata
english: "I give you eleven thousand horses, born in good lands, of noble breed, and of great vigor, O steadfast one.

sanskrit: nānāvarṇavibhaktānāṃ vayaḥsthānāṃ tathaiva ca dadāmy ekāṃ gavāṃ koṭiṃ śabalā dīyatāṃ mama
english: "I give you a full crore of cows distinguished by various colors and all in their prime; let Śabalā be given to me."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhagavān viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā na dāsyāmīti śabalāṃ prāha rājan kathaṃ cana
english: Thus addressed by the wise Viśvāmitra, the venerable Vasiṣṭha declared: "I will not give Śabalā under any circumstances whatsoever, O king."

sanskrit: etad eva hi me ratnam etad eva hi me dhanam etad eva hi sarvasvam etad eva hi jīvitam
english: "She alone is my jewel; she alone is my wealth; she alone is my all; she alone is my very life.

sanskrit: darśaś ca pūrṇamāsaś ca yajñāś caivāptadakṣiṇāḥ etad eva hi me rājan vividhāś ca kriyās tathā
english: "The new-moon sacrifice and the full-moon sacrifice, and the great sacrifices yielding abundant sacrificial fees—all these rest on her alone, O king, as do my various ritual observances.

sanskrit: adomūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā mama rājan na saṃśayaḥ bahūnāṃ kiṃ pralāpena na dāsye kāmadohinīm
english: "All my rites are rooted in her, O king—there is no doubt. Why speak at length? I will not give away the wish-granting cow."

sanskrit: kāmadhenuṃ vasiṣṭho 'pi yadā na tyajate muniḥ tadāsya śabalāṃ rāma viśvāmitro 'nvakarṣata
english: When the sage Vasiṣṭha would not surrender the wish-fulfilling cow, O Rāma, Viśvāmitra then dragged Śabalā away by force.

sanskrit: nīyamānā tu śabalā rāma rājñā mahātmanā duḥkhitā cintayām āsa rudantī śokakarśitā
english: But as Śabalā was being taken away, O Rāma, by that great-souled king, she was distressed; weeping and wasted by grief, she reflected.

sanskrit: parityaktā vasiṣṭhena kim ahaṃ sumahātmanā yāhaṃ rājabhṛtair dīnā hriyeyaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitā
english: "Why have I been abandoned by Vasiṣṭha, that most great-souled one? Why am I, wretched and deeply afflicted, being carried off by the king's servants?

sanskrit: kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ tasya maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ yan mām anāgasaṃ bhaktām iṣṭāṃ tyajati dhārmikaḥ
english: "What wrong have I done to that great sage of cultivated soul, that the righteous one abandons me who am guiltless, devoted, and dear to him?"

sanskrit: iti sā cintayitvā tu niḥśvasya ca punaḥ punaḥ jagāma vegena tadā vasiṣṭhaṃ paramaujasaṃ
english: Having reflected thus and sighing again and again, she then swiftly went back to Vasiṣṭha, who was of supreme power.

sanskrit: nirdhūya tāṃs tadā bhṛtyāñ śataśaḥ śatrusūdana jagāmānilavegena pādamūlaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Shaking off those hundreds of servants, O slayer of enemies, she went with the speed of the wind to the feet of the great-souled one.

sanskrit: śabalā sā rudantī ca krośantī cedam abravīt vasiṣṭhasyāgrataḥ sthitvā meghadundubhirāviṇī
english: Standing before Vasiṣṭha, that Śabalā, weeping and crying out, spoke these words with a voice resounding like a thunder-drum of clouds.

sanskrit: bhagavan kiṃ parityaktā tvayāhaṃ brahmaṇaḥ suta yasmād rājabhṛtā māṃ hi nayante tvatsakāśataḥ
english: "O venerable one, O son of Brahmā, why have I been abandoned by you? Why are the king's servants taking me away from your side?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu brahmarṣir idaṃ vacanam abravīt śokasaṃtaptahṛdayāṃ svasāram iva duḥkhitām
english: Addressed thus, the brahmarṣi spoke these words to her whose heart was burning with grief, as one would speak to a sorrowful sister.

sanskrit: na tvāṃ tyajāmi śabale nāpi me 'pakṛtaṃ tvayā eṣa tvāṃ nayate rājā balān matto mahābalaḥ
english: "I am not abandoning you, O Śabalā; nor have you done any wrong to me. This king of great might is taking you from me by force.

sanskrit: na hi tulyaṃ balaṃ mahyaṃ rājā tv adya viśeṣataḥ balī rājā kṣatriyaś ca pṛthivyāḥ patir eva ca
english: "My strength is simply not equal to his; the king today is particularly powerful—he is mighty, a kṣatriya, and lord of the earth.

sanskrit: iyam akṣauhiṇīpūrṇā savājirathasaṃkulā hastidhvajasamākīrṇā tenāsau balavattaraḥ
english: "This full akṣauhiṇī division of his, teeming with horses and chariots and thronged with elephants and banners—by reason of this he is the stronger."

sanskrit: evam uktā vasiṣṭhena pratyuvāca vinītavat vacanaṃ vacanajñā sā brahmarṣim amitaprabham
english: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, she who was skilled in speech replied humbly to the brahmarṣi of boundless splendor.

sanskrit: na balaṃ kṣatriyasyāhur brāhmaṇo balavattaraḥ brahman brahmabalaṃ divyaṃ kṣatrāt tu balavattaram
english: "The strength of a kṣatriya is not reckoned as strength; a brāhmaṇa is the stronger. O brāhmaṇa, brahmic power is divine and mightier than kṣatra-power.

sanskrit: aprameyabalaṃ tubhyaṃ na tvayā balavattaraḥ viśvāmitro mahāvīryas tejas tava durāsadam
english: "Your power is immeasurable; none is stronger than you. The mighty Viśvāmitra is no match for the splendor that is yours and difficult to approach.

sanskrit: niyuṅkṣva māṃ mahātejas tvadbrahmabalasaṃbhṛtām tasya darpaṃ balaṃ yat tan nāśayāmi durātmanaḥ
english: "O great-splendored one, employ me, filled as I am with your brahmic power; I shall destroy all the arrogance and strength of that wicked-souled one."

sanskrit: ity uktas tu tayā rāma vasiṣṭhaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ sṛjasveti tadovāca balaṃ parabalārujam
english: Thus addressed by her, O Rāma, Vasiṣṭha of great renown then said to her: "Create a force that shall break the power of the enemy."

sanskrit: tasyā humbhāravotsṛṣṭāḥ pahlavāḥ śataśo nṛpa nāśayanti balaṃ sarvaṃ viśvāmitrasya paśyataḥ
english: From her hum-bellowing, hundreds of Pahlavas were released, O king, and they destroyed Viśvāmitra's entire army even as he watched.

sanskrit: sa rājā paramakruddhaḥ krodhavisphāritekṣaṇaḥ pahlavān nāśayām āsa śastrair uccāvacair api
english: The king, exceedingly enraged, his eyes wide with fury, destroyed those Pahlavas with weapons of various kinds.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrārditān dṛṣṭvā pahlavāñ śataśas tadā bhūya evāsṛjad ghorāñ śakān yavanamiśritān
english: Seeing the hundreds of Pahlavas being crushed by Viśvāmitra, she again created fearsome Śakas mixed with Yavanas.

sanskrit: tair āsīt saṃvṛtā bhūmiḥ śakair yavanamiśritaiḥ prabhāvadbhir mahāvīryair hemakiñjalkasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: The earth was covered by those Śakas mixed with Yavanas, mighty and powerful, resembling the golden filaments of a lotus.

sanskrit: dīrghāsipaṭṭiśadharair hemavarṇāmbarāvṛtaiḥ nirdagdhaṃ tad balaṃ sarvaṃ pradīptair iva pāvakaiḥ
english: Bearing long swords and battle-axes, clad in garments of golden hue, they burned down that entire army like blazing fires.

sanskrit: tato 'strāṇi mahātejā viśvāmitro mumoca ha
english: Thereupon the great-splendored Viśvāmitra discharged his weapons.

sanskrit: tatas tān ākulān dṛṣṭvā viśvāmitrāstramohitān vasiṣṭhaś codayām āsa kāmadhuk sṛja yogataḥ
english: Then, seeing them thrown into confusion and bewildered by Viśvāmitra's weapons, Vasiṣṭha urged the wish-fulfilling cow: "Create with your yogic power."

sanskrit: tasyā humbhāravāj jātāḥ kāmbojā ravisaṃnibhāḥ ūdhasas tv atha saṃjātāḥ pahlavāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ
english: From her hum-bellow were born Kāmbojas bright as the sun; from her udder were then born Pahlavas bearing weapons in their hands.

sanskrit: yonideśāc ca yavanaḥ śakṛddeśāc chakās tathā romakūpeṣu mecchāś ca harītāḥ sakirātakāḥ
english: From her womb-region Yavanas, from her dung-region Śakas; from her pores barbarian Mlecchas, Harītas, and Kirātas together.

sanskrit: tais tan niṣūditaṃ sainyaṃ viśvamitrasya tatkṣaṇāt sapadātigajaṃ sāśvaṃ sarathaṃ raghunandana
english: By them Viśvāmitra's army was slaughtered that very instant—infantry, elephants, horses, and chariots—O delight of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā niṣūditaṃ sainyaṃ vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā viśvāmitrasutānāṃ tu śataṃ nānāvidhāyudham
english: Seeing the army destroyed by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, a hundred of Viśvāmitra's sons bearing weapons of every kind

sanskrit: abhyadhāvat susaṃkruddhaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ japatāṃ varam huṃkāreṇaiva tān sarvān nirdadāha mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: rushed furiously against Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of those who recite sacred texts; with a mere huṃkāra the great sage reduced them all to ashes.

sanskrit: te sāśvarathapādātā vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā bhasmīkṛtā muhūrtena viśvāmitrasutās tadā
english: Those sons of Viśvāmitra, along with their horses, chariots, and infantry, were reduced to ashes in a moment by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vināśitān putrān balaṃ ca sumahāyaśāḥ savrīḍaś cintayāviṣṭo viśvāmitro 'bhavat tadā
english: Seeing his sons and his army destroyed, the greatly renowned Viśvāmitra became filled with shame and was plunged into despondency.

sanskrit: saṃdura iva nirvego bhagnadaṃṣṭra ivoragaḥ uparakta ivādityaḥ sadyo niṣprabhatāṃ gataḥ
english: Like a river that has lost its current, like a serpent with broken fangs, like the sun at the moment of an eclipse—he instantly lost his radiance.

sanskrit: hataputrabalo dīno lūnapakṣa iva dvijaḥ hatadarpo hatotsāho nirvedaṃ samapadyata
english: With his sons and army slain, wretched like a bird with clipped wings, his arrogance destroyed, his energy extinguished, he fell into dejection.

sanskrit: sa putram ekaṃ rājyāya pālayeti niyujya ca pṛthivīṃ kṣatradharmeṇa vanam evānvapadyata
english: He appointed one son to the kingdom with the charge "rule it," to govern the earth according to kṣatriya duty, and then he departed to the forest.

sanskrit: sa gatvā himavatpārśvaṃ kiṃnaroragasevitam mahādevaprasādārthaṃ tapas tepe mahātapāḥ
english: Going to the slopes of the Himavat, frequented by Kiṃnaras and serpents, he of great austerities performed tapas in order to propitiate Mahādeva.

sanskrit: kena cit tv atha kālena deveśo vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ darśayām āsa varado viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim
english: After some time had passed, the lord of the gods, he whose banner bears a bull, the granter of boons, appeared before the great sage Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ tapyase rājan brūhi yat te vivakṣitam varado 'smi varo yas te kāṅkṣitaḥ so 'bhidhīyatām
english: "For what purpose do you practice austerities, O king? Speak what you wish to say. I am a granter of boons; declare whatever boon you desire."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu devena viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ praṇipatya mahādevam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the god, Viśvāmitra of great austerities bowed down to Mahādeva and spoke these words.

sanskrit: yadi tuṣṭo mahādeva dhanurvedo mamānagha sāṅgopāṅgopaniṣadaḥ sarahasyaḥ pradīyatām
english: "If you are pleased with me, O Mahādeva, O sinless one, let the Dhanurveda be given to me in its entirety—with all its subsidiary texts, upāṅgas, upaniṣads, and its secret doctrine."

sanskrit: yāni deveṣu cāstrāṇi dānaveṣu maharṣiṣu gandharvayakṣarakṣaḥsu pratibhāntu mamānagha
english: "And let all the weapons that are among the gods, the Dānavas, the great sages, the Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas—let all of these manifest themselves to me, O sinless one."

sanskrit: tava prasādād bhavatu devadeva mamepsitam evam astv iti deveśo vākyam uktvā divaṃ gataḥ
english: "By your grace let my desire be fulfilled, O god of gods." Having spoken the words "so be it," the lord of the gods departed to heaven.

sanskrit: prāpya cāstrāṇi rājarṣir viśvāmitro mahābalaḥ darpeṇa mahatā yukto darpapūrṇo 'bhavat tadā
english: Having obtained the weapons, the royal sage Viśvāmitra of great might became filled with arrogance and swelled with immense pride.

sanskrit: vivardhamāno vīryeṇa samudra iva parvaṇi hatam eva tadā mene vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam
english: Growing in his might like the ocean at the full moon, he then considered the foremost of sages, Vasiṣṭha, as already slain.

sanskrit: tato gatvāśramapadaṃ mumocāstrāṇi pārthivaḥ yais tat tapovanaṃ sarvaṃ nirdagdhaṃ cāstratejasā
english: Then the king went to the hermitage and discharged his weapons, by which that entire grove of austerities was burned down by the power of those weapons.

sanskrit: udīryamāṇam astraṃ tad viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ dṛṣṭvā vipradrutā bhītā munayaḥ śataśaḥ diśaḥ
english: Seeing that weapon of the wise Viśvāmitra blazing forth, hundreds of sages fled in terror in all directions.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasya ca ye śiṣyās tathaiva mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ vidravanti bhayād bhītā nānādigbhyaḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: And the disciples of Vasiṣṭha, as well as the deer and birds, fled in fear by the thousands in many directions.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasyāśramapadaṃ śūnyam āsīn mahātmanaḥ muhūrtam iva niḥśabdam āsīd īriṇasaṃnibham
english: The hermitage of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha became deserted; for a moment it was silent, resembling a barren wasteland.

sanskrit: vadato vai vasiṣṭhasya mā bhaiṣṭeti muhur muhuḥ nāśayāmy adya gādheyaṃ nīhāram iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha called out repeatedly: "Fear not! I shall destroy Gādheya today as the sun dispels the mist."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā vasiṣṭho japatāṃ varaḥ viśvāmitraṃ tadā vākyaṃ saroṣam idam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus, the great-splendored Vasiṣṭha, the foremost among those who recite sacred texts, then addressed Viśvāmitra in these angry words.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ cirasaṃvṛddhaṃ yad vināśitavān asi durācāro 'si yan mūḍha tasmāt tvaṃ na bhaviṣyasi
english: "Because you have destroyed this hermitage nurtured for so long, you are a man of wicked conduct; because of this, O fool, you shall be no more."

sanskrit: ity uktvā paramakruddho daṇḍam udyamya satvaraḥ vidhūma iva kālāgnir yamadaṇḍam ivāparam
english: Having spoken thus, supremely enraged, he swiftly raised his staff—like the smokeless fire of universal dissolution, like another rod of Yama.
